lines: The spiral descent ends in a circular chamber identical in structure to the Spire of Vigil's core — but alive with motion. Wind spirals up from vents in the floor, following invisible channels that make the air itself glow.

The geometric patterns on every surface pulse with blue-white light, cycling in rhythm with your sol unit. The Spire recognizes the technology — and the activation of its sister structure in the Nightside.
At the center, a crystal pedestal rises from the floor. Unlike Vigil's dark stillness, this one hums with barely contained energy. The wind currents converge on it from every direction.
You place your hand on the crystal pedestal. The wind stops. Every current, every breeze, every whisper of air in the chamber freezes in place.
Then it reverses. Wind crashes inward from every direction, channeling through the geometric grooves, converging on your sol unit with a force that lifts you off the ground.

For a heartbeat you hover — weightless, suspended by forces the Spire's builders mastered millennia ago. Your sol unit drinks in the energy, its housing reconfiguring around a new capability that rewrites its relationship with gravity itself.

The wind releases you gently. But the knowledge remains, etched into your sol unit's core architecture. You can feel it — the ability to defy the ground beneath you, to rise above obstacles, to navigate vertical space as easily as horizontal.
HOVER UNLOCKED — activate anti-gravity thrusters to float above the ground, changing elevation levels and crossing chasms.

actions.text: Return to Councillor Asha Denn with the Spire data
The pedestal hums quietly. The Spire's gift has been given. The wind currents still flow, but gently now — the core is at rest.
The Spire offers a final gift — ancient components preserved in crystal, designed for technology that wouldn't exist for millennia after the Spire was built.
The cache is sealed in crystal. The resonance pedestal must be activated first.
The resonance core pulses with gentle wind. The Spire of Winds has fulfilled its purpose. Above, the Bulwark's fortress feels very far away — and very small.
